yeah, looks like a bug to me.

I not sure : 
@vsavkin writes in his book : "Finally, the router will call the canLoad guard during any navigation loading contacts, not just the first time, even though the bundle itself will be loaded only once"
That, I don't know. For me, canLoad is use  for testing permissions. Permissions can change at any time.

That, I don't know. For me, canLoad is use for testing permissions.
Permissions can change at any time.

Isn't that the role of CanActivate? CanLoad is for loading and CanActivate
for activating. And I think the official guide about routing says so too...
(On my phone, so I can't give a link right now).

> CanLoad
Sometimes, for security reasons, we do not want the user to be able to even see the source code of the lazily loaded bundle if she does not have the right permissions. That’s what the canLoad guard is for. If a canLoad guard returns false, the router will not load the bundle.

> CanActivate
The canActivate guard is the default mechanism of adding permissions to the application.
@vsavkin once a route has been loaded it seems that the guard should not be called any more ?

This citation comes from the vsavkin's book. vsavkin is the architect  in charge of router. 

> after loaded once by the client, the bundle content is visible, so there is no need for revalidating authorization for loading, you can't make the bundle disappear from the client.

I agree with that. Probably, It misses a state in this case.

@vicb any news on this issue? I think it should be good to fix it before releasing the 4.0.0 at least since it may be breaking (or should I say unbreaking) things…
By the way, from memory, it is actually a regression bug, since in the past, canload wasn't called everytime I think and this changed in one of the versions of 2.x… (not 100% sure about that though :)
@victornoel just add a boolean flag and set it to true after the first invocation
@DzmitryShylovich I already do that, I was more worried about the underlying problem of interpreting the semantics of `CanLoad` for the benefit of the Angular community :)
